title: Closure Figures for the Northbeam Credit Products
content:
An account of the Northbeam Store Credit and Financing Accounts range ends on figures its own product sets: the days of notice the retailer gives before closing an account for inactivity, the months without a transaction after which the account is closed, and what happens to a balance on a closing account.

| Product | Days of notice before closing for inactivity | Months without a transaction after which the account is closed | What happens to a balance on a closing account |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northbeam Store Card | 45 | 24 | the balance stays payable at the same rate until cleared |
| Northbeam Store Card Plus | 45 | 24 | the balance stays payable at the same rate until cleared |
| Northbeam Signature Rewards Card | 45 | 36 | the balance stays payable at the same rate until cleared |
| Northbeam Deferred Interest Promotion Account | 45 | 18 | any deferred interest becomes payable at once |
| Northbeam Business Net Thirty Account | 60 | 24 | the outstanding invoices stay payable on their terms |
| Northbeam Business Fleet Line of Credit | 90 | 36 | the outstanding invoices stay payable on their terms |

Days and months are as stated; the third column is the basis the product itself sets.

## Notes

1. The notice period is 45 days on all four consumer products, 60 days on the Northbeam Business Net Thirty Account and 90 days on the Northbeam Business Fleet Line of Credit.
2. The inactivity period is counted in months without a transaction. It is shortest on the Northbeam Deferred Interest Promotion Account at 18 months, stands at 24 months on the Northbeam Store Card, the Northbeam Store Card Plus and the Northbeam Business Net Thirty Account, and runs to 36 months on the Northbeam Signature Rewards Card and the Northbeam Business Fleet Line of Credit. An account on the 18-month product reaches that period a year and a half after its last transaction, half the time the 36-month products allow.
3. The three bases in the last column differ in kind: the three cards keep the balance payable at the same rate until it is cleared, the deferred interest product brings its accrued interest forward to be payable at once, and the two business products leave the outstanding invoices payable on the terms they were raised under.
